takeaways: Moderna swung to a $0.38 profit vs Wall Street's expected $1.25 loss, on $1.31 billion of revenue vs $885.1 million expected (LSEG via CNBC) — a roughly 48% revenue beat.
Sales jumped 29% year over year, with $780 million in the U.S. and $533 million internationally, helped by COVID vaccine deliveries under long-term government partnerships abroad.
Full-year 2026 revenue growth guidance went to 15%–25% from 'up to 10%,' R&D spend outlook fell to about $2.7 billion from $2.9 billion, and year-end cash is now seen at $8.1–$8.3 billion.
CEO Stéphane Bancel told CNBC newer products and geographic expansion (Canada, U.K., Asia) drove the quarter, and cost cuts helped the return to profit.

The company also highlighted U.S. approval of its flu shot mFLUSIVA and positive Phase 3 melanoma data for intismeran with Merck — though the stock had sold off earlier when some of that cancer data leaked.
verdict: Wall Street showed up expecting another red quarter and Moderna handed it a green one, by a mile. International COVID contracts and a leaner cost base turned a predicted $1.25 loss into 38 cents of profit, then management hiked the sales outlook. Max's take: the mRNA story just reminded everyone it can still print money when the shots ship.
